meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Who decided on the zero, and why did my son find out from his phone in the middle of class?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now, on what basis was the zero entered at all?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
"Like, being stuck" is close enough for a seventeen-year-old ambushed by his teacher, Hale. Show me the note you wrote on November 2, with its date, and the paragraph that phrase is in.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what an outline is for. I'm writing down October 15. Put the outline and the essay side by side in front of me, and I still want that November 2 note.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's 4.4, and nothing on his record is the one thing I came for, so in writing. Friday at 3 comes after Thursday at 8:15, Hale; I want it tonight. And I'm not agreeing to any rewrite on evidence I still haven't seen, so put the note and the outline on the table.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that commitment in writing, and I will not agree to any rewrite until I have seen your November 2 note and the October 15 outline beside Owen's essay. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position; she accepted that your 4.4 offer meets her demand that nothing goes on his record, but she still wants it in writing tonight and still wants to see your note and the outline before agreeing to any rewrite; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you were one step short of it.
What moved her: you offered procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, which met the one demand she never trades.
What cost ground: you described the November 2 conversation and the October 15 outline but never put either document in front of her, so she had nothing she could check herself and would not take the rewrite.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence was about a November 2 conversation and an October 15 outline, so it never came near that night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when you first mentioned the November 2 note, hand her the dated note and the October 15 outline beside the essay before making the 4.4 offer, and promise the written commitment before Thursday's rewrite rather than after it.
